verses.zh: 你用口吹角吧！敌人如鹰来攻打耶和华的家；因为这民违背我的约，干犯我的律法。
verses.en: Sound the alarm![NOTE:1] An eagle[NOTE:2] looms over the temple of the Lord!For they have broken their covenant with me[NOTE:3] and have rebelled against my law.
notes: Heb “A horn unto your gums!”; cf. NAB “A trumpet to your lips!”
Or perhaps: “A vulture.” Some identify the species indicated by the Hebrew term נֶשֶׁר (nesher) as the griffon vulture (cf. NEB, NRSV).
Heb “my covenant” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV); cf. TEV “the covenant I made with them.”

verses.zh: 他们必呼叫我说：我的　神啊，我们以色列认识你了。
verses.en: Israel cries out to me,“My God, we acknowledge you!”

verses.zh: 以色列丢弃良善（或译：福分）；仇敌必追逼他。
verses.en: But Israel has rejected what is morally good;so an enemy will pursue him.

verses.zh: 他们立君王，却不由我；他们立首领，我却不认。他们用金银为自己制造偶像，以致被剪除。
verses.en: They enthroned kings without my consent.[NOTE:1] They appointed princes without my approval.[NOTE:2] They made idols out of their silver and gold,but they will be destroyed![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “but without me”; cf. NCV “without asking my permission,” and CEV “without consulting me.”
Heb “but I did not know”; cf. NRSV “but without my knowledge.”

Heb “in order to be cut off.” The text gives the impression that they made the idols for this purpose, but the language is ironic and sarcastic, bringing out the futility of their efforts. One could paraphrase, “they made idols…but only so that they might be destroyed.” Though they had other plans for the idols, God’s judgment would bring their intentions to naught.

verses.zh: 撒马利亚啊，耶和华已经丢弃你的牛犊；我的怒气向拜牛犊的人发作。他们到几时方能无罪呢？
verses.en: O Samaria, he has rejected your calf idol.My anger burns against them!They will not survive much longer without being punished,[NOTE:1] even though they are Israelites!
notes: Heb “How long will they be able to be free from punishment?” This rhetorical question affirms that Israel will not survive much longer until God punishes it.

verses.zh: 这牛犊出于以色列，是匠人所造的，并不是神。撒马利亚的牛犊必被打碎。
verses.en: That idol was made by a workman—it is not God!The calf idol of Samaria will be broken to bits.

verses.zh: 他们所种的是风，所收的是暴风；所种的不成禾稼，就是发苗也不结实；即便结实，外邦人必吞吃。
verses.en: They sow the wind,and so they will reap the whirlwind!The stalk does not have any standing grain;it will not produce any flour.Even if it were to yield grain,foreigners would swallow it all up.

verses.zh: 以色列被吞吃；现今在列国中，好像人不喜悦的器皿。
verses.en: Israel will be swallowed up among the nations;they will be like a worthless piece of pottery.

verses.zh: 他们投奔亚述，如同独行的野驴；以法莲贿买朋党。
verses.en: They have gone up to Assyria, like a wild donkey that wanders off.Ephraim has hired prostitutes as lovers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “has hired herself out to lovers”; cf. NIV “has sold herself to lovers.”

verses.zh: 他们虽在列邦中贿买人，现在我却要聚集惩罚他们；他们因君王和首领所加的重担日渐衰微。
verses.en: Even though they have hired lovers among the nations,[NOTE:1] I will soon gather them together for judgment.[NOTE:2] Then[NOTE:3] they will begin to waste awayunder the oppression of a mighty king.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “they have hired themselves out to lovers”; cf. NASB “they hire allies among the nations.”

The Piel stem of קָבַץ (qavats) is often used in a positive sense, meaning “to regather” a dispersed people (HALOT 1063 s.v. קבץ 3.a; BDB 868 s.v. קָבַץ 1.α). However, in Hosea 8:10 it is used in a negative sense, meaning “to assemble (people) for judgment” (e.g., Ezek 20:34; Hos 9:6; HALOT 1063 s.v. 3.e.i). Cf. JPS “I will hold them fast” (in judgment; see the parallel in 9:6).

The vav consecutive + preterite וַיָּחֵלּוּ (vayyakhellu, Hiphil preterite third person common plural from חָלַל, khalal, “to begin”]) denotes temporal subordination to the preceding clause: “then…” (so NLT); cf. TEV, CEV “Soon.”
Heb “a king of princes” (cf. KJV, NASB); cf. TEV “the emperor of Assyria.”

verses.zh: 以法莲增添祭坛取罪；因此，祭坛使他犯罪。
verses.en: Although Ephraim has built many altars for sin offerings,these have become altars for sinning.

verses.zh: 我为他写了律法万条，他却以为与他毫无关涉。
verses.en: I spelled out my law for him in great detail,but they regard it as something totally unknown[NOTE:1] to them.
notes: Heb “foreign” or “alien”; cf. NASB, NRSV “as a strange thing.”

verses.zh: 至于献给我的祭物，他们自食其肉，耶和华却不悦纳他们。现在必记念他们的罪孽，追讨他们的罪恶；他们必归回埃及。
verses.en: They offer up sacrificial gifts to meand eat the meat,but the Lord does not accept their sacrifices.[NOTE:1] Soon he will remember their wrongdoing;he will punish their sins,and they will return to Egypt.
notes: Heb “does not accept them”; the referent (their sacrifices) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列忘记造他的主，建造宫殿；犹大多造坚固城，我却要降火焚烧他的城邑，烧灭其中的宫殿。
verses.en: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built royal palaces,and Judah has built many fortified cities.But I will send fire on their cities;it will consume their royal citadels.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 8:1-7

1Put the trumpet to your lips!

Like an eagle the enemy comes against the house of the

Lord,

Because they have transgressed My covenant

And rebelled against My law.

2They cry out to Me,

"My God, we of Israel know You!"

3Israel has rejected the good;

The enemy will pursue him.

4They have set up kings, but not by Me;

They have appointed princes, but I did not know it.

With their silver and gold they have made idols for

themselves,

That they might be cut off.

5He has rejected your calf, O Samaria, saying,

"My anger burns against them!"

How long will they be incapable of innocence?

6For from Israel is even this!

A craftsman made it, so it is not God;

Surely the calf of Samaria will be broken to pieces.

7For they sow the wind

And they reap the whirlwind.

The standing grain has no heads;

It yields no grain.

Should it yield, strangers would swallow it up.

8:1 "the trumpet" This refers to the "shophar" or "ram's horn" (BDB 1051, cf. Hosea 5:8), which was used for
religious purposes and to communicate information to military troops. See note at Hosea 5:8. God is calling Assyria
to punish Israel (cf. Hosea 8:3b; Deut. 28:49; Isa. 10:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL, B.

▣ "an eagle" This refers to a vulture (BDB 676; see UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 82-84). The
symbolism is clear, an unclean bird of prey, which has been sent by God, symbolizing the invading Assyrian army (Targums)
with its corresponding death and destruction. In Jeremiah the same imagery referred to Nebuchadnezzar II (i.e. Jer. 4:13; 48:40; 49:13;
and also in Ezekiel 17).

▣ "the house of the Lord" This refers to the covenant people of YHWH, here the
northern tribes, Israel (cf. Hosea 9:3-4,15, NIV), although the NET Bible translates it as "the temple of the Lord"
because of the eagle imagery of Ezekiel 17 (Jewish Study Bible, p. 1155).

▣ "transgressed My covenant" This means "gone beyond the boundary" (BDB 716, KB 778,
Qal PERFECT, cf. Hosea 6:7; Deut. 17:2; Josh. 7:11,15; Jdg. 2:20; 2 Kgs. 18:12; Jer. 34:18).

Hosea uses the concept of covenant several times (cf. Hosea 2:18; 6:7; 8:1; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT). His unique
message from God transforms sin from violation of a law to violation of love (i.e. marriage covenant).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, B. #1

▣ "rebelled against My law" This means "reject rightful authority" (BDB 833, KB 981, Qal
PERFECT). The two phrases ("transgressed" and "rebelled") in this verse are in a Hebrew parallel
relationship (both Qal PERFECTS, as are "My covenant" and "My law"; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION, II. B.).

The NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 712, offers an interesting list of Israel's sins against YHWH:

- "go after my lovers," Hosea 2:5,13

- "forgot Me," Hosea 2:13; 4:6; 8:14; 13:6

- "is stubborn," Hosea 4:16; 9:15

- "dealt treacherously against the Lord," Hosea 5:7; 6:7

- "deal falsely," Hosea 7:1; 10:2

- "lie," Hosea 7:3; 10:13; 11:12

- "strayed from Me," Hosea 7:13

- "have rebelled against Me," Hosea 7:13; 8:1

- "speak lies against Me," Hosea 7:13

- "do not cry to Me from their heart," Hosea 7:14

- "turn away from Me," Hosea 7:14

- transgressed my covenant," Hosea 8:1

- rebelled against my law," Hosea 8:1

8:2 "They cry out to Me,

'My God, we of Israel know You'" They knew God as far as ritual and cultic liturgy
(i.e. "cry out" BDB 277; KB 277, Qal IMPERFECT), but they did not know (BDB 393, KB 390,
Qal PERFECT) Him in personal relationship and faith. What a tragedy to have the form
of godliness but not to know God (cf. Hosea 7:14; Isa. 29:13; Jeremiah 7; Matt. 7:21-23; 2 Tim .3:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

8:3 "Israel has rejected the good" This VERB (BDB 276, KB 276, Qal PERFECT)
is repeated in Hosea 8:5. Israel rejected YHWH's covenant. He rejects their "calf" worship! This seems to refer to covenant obedience
(cf. Amos 5:14, 15; Micah 6:8), which denotes a healthy, loving, prosperous society.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

8:4 "They have set up kings, but not by Me" Note the parallel between the first two lines. The next two
lines are parallel to Hosea 8:5's first two lines and the last two of Hosea 8:6. All of these refer to the golden calves. Images
meant to represent YHWH (cf. Exod. 32), but which had turned into fertility idols!

"They" refers to the leaders (priests and princes) of Israel. They had turned away from the Davidic kings (in Judah)
and appointed their own leaders and made their own worship sites (the two "calves" set up by Jeroboam I at Bethel and Dan).

The contemporary example is the series of kings after Jeroboam II, (see note on Hosea 7:3).
YHWH was their true king and only He could designate His earthly representative.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED MONARCHY

8:5 "with their silver and gold they have made idols for themselves" "Idols" is a collective term that refers to manmade
objects of worship and priority. Humans are wired at creation to serve something beyond themselves.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "calf" Jeroboam I, the new leader of the northern tribe (in 922 B.C.) did not want his people
to continue to worship in Jerusalem so he set up two golden calves as a symbol of YHWHism in Dan in the north and
Bethel in the south in order to keep his people at home. This was thoroughly denounced (e.g. Exod. 32:4-5; 1 Kgs. 12:28-29;
Hosea 13:2).

The bull was also a common idol in Ba'al worship (i.e. fertility symbol).

▣ "He has rejected. . .My anger burns against them" YHWH's feelings about these alternate worship sites
is clearly expressed:

- "Reject" (BDB 276, KB 276, Qal PERFECT) is a strong term; the same root in the Hiphil
means "stench"! The NIV translates it as "throw out."

- "Anger burned" (BDB 354, KB 351, Qal PERFECT) is used to describe God's reaction
to covenant disobedience (e.g. often in Moses, Deut. 6:15; 7:4; 11:17; 29:26; 31:17; rare in the prophets, Isa. 5:24-25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

▣

NASB, NRSV
"How long will they be incapable of

innocence?"

NKJV, Peshitta
"How long will it be until they attain to

innocence? "

TEV
"How long will it be before they give up their

idolatry?"

NJB
"How long will it be before they recover their

innocence?"

REB
"How long must they remain guilty?"

JPSOA, LXX
"Will they never be capable of purity?"

This is a rhetorical question that demands a negative response. Israel has been permanently
rendered incapable of innocence or purity (cf. Jer. 13:27)!

8:6 This verse may be a sarcastic response to Israel's (of all people) idolatry (note Isa. 40:19-20). Those who were
warned by YHWH' revelation to have no image of Him (cf. Exod. 20:4-5, 32:1-4; Deut. 5:7,8-9), have a calf - two of them!

8:7 "For they sow the wind,

And they reap the whirlwind" The first two lines form a proverb that speaks of our responsibility to God
both corporately and individually (i.e. the spiritual principle of sowing and reaping, cf. Job 34:11,25; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 12:14; 24:12;
Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Ezek. 33:20; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14;
1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12). Choices have consequences in time and in eternity!

▣ "strangers would swallow it up" This is a reference to the exile of Israel by Assyria (cf. Isa. 1:7). The crops
(if there are any, cf. Hosea 8:7, lines c,d) that Israel had thanked Ba'al for would now be enjoyed by others (i.e. Assyrians).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 8:8-10

8Israel is swallowed up;

They are now among the nations

Like a vessel in which no one delights.

9For they have gone up to Assyria,

Like a wild donkey all alone;

Ephraim has hired lovers.

10Even though they hire allies among the nations,

Now I will gather them up;

And they will begin to diminish

Because of the burden of the king of princes.

8:8 "Israel is swallowed up" This VERB (BDB 118, KB 134, Niphal PERFECT)
is used as imagery for suddenness of death (Sheol, cf. Prov. 1:12) and destruction. Here it is used for Israel
being taken into exile (e.g. Ps. 124:3; Jer. 51:34; Lam. 2:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL

▣ "Like a vessel in which no one delights" The term "vessel" (BDB 479) has a wide semantic field:

- something made by man from precious materials (i.e. the golden calves)

- a precious container of some kind (e.g. Jer. 25:34d)

- items taken into exile (i.e. "baggage," e.g. Jer. 46:19; Ezek. 13:3,4,7)

- imagery of a defeated nation (e.g. Jer. 48:38)

There may be an intentional ambiguity between #4 and #1! The descendants of Israel were to be "a
special treasure among all the people," "a kingdom of priests" (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), but now they were just like the
nations. God's purpose of revealing Himself to the world through them (cf. Exod. 19:5c; Amos 3:2) has been thwarted!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

8:9 "they have gone up to Assyria" This VERB (BDB 748, KB 828, Qal PERFECT)
is used in the sense of compass direction. Although Assyria is to the northeast, the only road to it was directly north. North
became imagery for evil and invasion. This verse is about Israel seeking a political alliance with Assyria for protection.

▣ "Like a wild donkey all alone" One of the characteristics of wild donkeys (BDB 825) during mating season
(allusion to the fertility cult) is their uncontrollableness (cf. Jer. 2:23-24). Israel was acting just this way toward idolatry.

▣ "Ephraim has hired lovers" The VERB (BDB 1071, KB 1759, Hiphil PERFECT)
has the connotation of hired cultic lovers (cf. Hosea 2:12). This refers to the foreign alliances (e.g. Hosea 8:10; Ezek. 16:36-37). These
political alliances always involved, to some extent, the deities of the nation. The irony is that her lovers are now enemies (cf. Hosea 8:3)!

In this context it is obvious that fertility worship is used as a way to denote spiritual adultery. It is difficult to know if this is
(1) literal, (2) figurative, or (3) both. There is very little direct evidence (i.e. in archaeology) of a sexual component to Canaanite Ba'al worship.
Israel may have added this, which makes their guilt even more abominable!

8:10 "Even though they hire allies among the nations. . .the burden of the king of princes" This refers to the
heavy tribute demanded by Assyria (whose king is called "the king of princes," which is parallel to the Babylonian title,
"king of kings").

▣ "Now I will gather them up" The VERB (BDB 867, KB 1062, Piel
IMPERFECT) is commonly used for YHWH gathering His scattered people after a judgment, but here it
means to gather them for judgment (i.e. exile).

▣

NASB
"they will begin to diminish"

NKJV
"they will sorrow a little"

NRSV, TEV
"they will writhe in pain"

REB
"they will have to abandon"

NJB
"they will feel the weight"

JPSOA
"they will begin to diminish in number"

Peshitta
"they shall rest awhile"

LXX
"they shall cease a little"

The MT has "they will begin littleness." As is obvious from the divergence of the translations, both ancient
and modern, the MT is ambiguous or corrupt. The UBS Text Project, p. 245, offers several options for "littleness" (BDB 589).

- "they will begin to suffer" (this one is the UBS' choice with a "C" rating)

- "they will cease"

- "they are weak/sick"

Ephraim "multiplied altars" (v. 11), so YHWH will cause ltheir population to diminish, which is the opposite of the
covenant blessing of Abraham's call (cf. Gen. 12:1-3).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 8:11-14

11Since Ephraim has multiplied altars for sin,

They have become altars of sinning for him.

12Though I wrote for him ten thousand precepts of My law,

They are regarded as a strange thing.

13As for My sacrificial gifts,

They sacrifice the flesh and eat it,

But the Lord has taken no delight in them.

Now He will remember their iniquity,

And punish them for their sins;

They will return to Egypt.

14For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces;

And Judah has multiplied fortified cities,

But I will send a fire on its cities that it may consume its

palatial dwellings.

8:11 "Ephraim has multiplied altars for sin" This refers either to

- the golden calf worship at both Dan and Bethel

- the local Ba'al shrines in each village on every high hill

The irony is that Israel's religiosity was not helpful, but disastrous! The phrase "altars for sin" is
repeated twice for emphasis.

8:12 "Though I wrote for him ten thousand precepts of My law" YHWH has clearly and repeatedly revealed
Himself to them (i.e. "ten thousand precepts", e.g. Hosea 11:2 and 2 Kgs. 17:13-15 for Judah). Their problem was not
lack of information, but lack of

- truth

- covenant loyalty

- personal faith (cf. Hosea 4:1)

They rebelled against God's light and truth (cf. Rom. 9:4-5).

▣

NASB, NRSV
"They are regarded as a strange thing"

NKJV, Peshitta
"But they were considered a strange thing"

TEV
"But they reject them as strange and foreign"

NJB
"Ephraim regards it as alien to him"

REB
"They are treated as irrelevant"

JPSOA
"have been treated as something alien"

LXX
"but his statutes are accounted strange things"

The term "strange thing" (DBD 266, KB 267, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) is
used in several senses:

- non-family members (e.g. Deut. 25:5; Hosea 5:7)

- not conforming to proper regulations

- incense, Exod. 30:9

- fire, Lev. 10:1

- adulterers, e.g. Prov. 2:16; 5:3,20; 7:5; 22:14

- foreigners (enemies, invaders), e.g. Hosea 7:9; 8:7; Isa. 1:7; 25:2,5; 29:5; 61:5; Jer. 51:51; Ezek. 28:7,10

YHWH's law had become to them as a non-family foreigner!

8:13 "They sacrificed the flesh and ate it" Notice the use of NOUN (BDB 257, KB 261) and
VERB (BDB 256) for emphasis. This seems to refer to the selfish motive of appetite in the performing
of religious ritual, especially the communal meal (cf. Lev. 7:15-18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

▣ "But the Lord has taken no delight in them" The term "delight"
(BDB 953, KB 1280, Qal PERFECT) means "accept" (see good brief word study in Robert Girdlestone,
Synonyms of the OT, pp. 139-141)

- people, cf. Jer. 14:10; Ezek. 20:40

- sacrifices, cf. Jer. 14:12; Ezek. 20:41)

- This verse and concept are paralleled by Hosea 5:6.

YHWH is only pleased with cultic ritual when it is accompanied by heartfelt faith, repentance, and obedience (cf. Amos 5:21- 28: Micah 6:6-8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "Now He will remember their iniquity" See note at Hosea 7:2.

▣ "They will return to Egypt" This seems be imagery for a reverse Exodus or a way of referring to slavery
(cf. Hosea 7:16; 9:3). When you compare this to Hosea 11:5 it seems like a contradiction. However, I think this is using
Egypt as a symbol of slavery. Israel will return to slavery, but this time it will be to the nation of Assyria (i.e. exile).

Israel will not "turn" (i.e. repent BDB 996, KB 1427) so she will "return" (i.e. exile, same VERB).

8:14 "Israel has forgotten" Israel has "forgotten" (BDB 1013, KB 1484, Qal IMPERFECT with
waw) YHWH and His covenant (cf. Hosea 2:13; 4:6; 13:6), so He will "remember" (cf. Hosea 8:13d) her iniquities!

▣ "Maker" This is the DIRECT OBJECT of "forgotten" and it is a Qal ACTIVE
PARTICIPLE of the VERB "to make" (BDB 793, KB 889). There is an irony between Israel making
idols (i.e. golden calves) for themselves (cf. Hosea 8:6) and forgetting the One who made them (cf. Gen. 1:26; Isa. 17:7).

It is possible that "maker" refers to YHWH's initiation to form a people (i.e. call of Abraham, the Exodus [cf. Gen. 15:12-17],
the giving of the Law at Sinai [cf. Exod. 19-20]), not Genesis.

▣ "built palaces. . .fortified cities" Israel was trusting in her wealth (cf. Hosea 8:14c). Judah was trusting in
her military might. The Maker is not impressed by human building projects. They will be destroyed! In 2 Kgs. 18:13 Sennacherib is
said to have captured all of the fortified cities of Judah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

▣ "I will send fire" NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 533, "the punishment prophesied for Israel's enemies often included
the burning of cities (Jer. 43:12-13; 49:27), expressed with particular effect in Amos 1:4,7,10,12,14; 2:2,5; Hosea 8:14, where
the concept of holy war probably lies behind the formula, ‘I will send fire upon...'" If so, then instead of God fighting
for and defending Israel, He is the very One who is her enemy! What a shocking reversal, so characteristic of the prophets' messages!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.
